result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers get the counts right and quote the tickets accurately. B is better: it lists all five themes separately with counts and bars, gives a clear bottom line based on ticket counts, and keeps what customers said apart from what the team should do. A puts suggested actions inside each finding and lumps lateness and the missing sock into one 'service issues' group. Neither visible part says that the counts only reflect people who wrote to support in one week, and both screenshots are cut off, so B's action list could not be checked. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A's counts match the data exactly (4, 2, 1, 1, 1), it keeps findings apart from conclusions, and its light layout with a clear order of importance works well as a page to send the team. B's counts are also correct, but it merges lateness and the missing item into one 'Service issues: 2' tile and puts its suggested actions inside the findings, so it doesn't separate what the tickets say from the ranked decisions. Neither visible screenshot says that these are only people who wrote to support in one week, so the counts don't show how common each problem is; both quote the tickets accurately and invent nothing.
